title: rtl-files.json — per-child RTL file layout (authored by assemble from the reaped child reports)
description: Which files each child wrote and which include directories they `include from. Every downstream filelist is GENERATED from this: simulation's rtl_filelist.f, synthesis's rtl_load.tcl, lint-cdc's scripts/filelist.txt. Keys are manifest child names, in manifest order. files[] order within a child is the child's declared dependency order — the child authors it and owns that claim. The order ACROSS children carries no dependency claim; it comes from the manifest so that it is stable no matter which children a round re-dispatched. A macro `define'd in one child and used in another is therefore not ordered correctly by it: cross-file macros belong in a header reached through incdirs, which is order-independent. An empty object is a legitimate transient state before wave 2 has reaped any child; the roster requirement lives in the post exit gate.

files.description: Paths relative to the rtl-design stage root, in dependency order. The child authors its own file layout — specification defines RTL modules, not files. The `.v`/`.vh` pattern is load-bearing rather than stylistic: the kernel's downstream `rtl` selectors match `*.v` alone, so a `.sv` artifact silently drops out of the derived dependency graph and its edits stop invalidating downstream proofs. Enforced here because write_ledger validates before the first write, so a bad extension can never reach disk for a later run to seed from.

incdirs.description: Include directories the child's files `include from, relative to the rtl-design stage root. Omitted or empty when the child uses no `include. Downstream emits these in each tool's own syntax; they are never joined into a text line for a reader to split apart again.
